schools.name: Early Merkavah and Hekhalot Literature
schools.focus: Visionary ascents through seven celestial palaces (Hekhalot) to behold the Divine Chariot (Merkavah) described in Ezekiel 1; Shi'ur Qomah anthropomorphic divine measurements.

schools.name: Sefer Yetzirah (Book of Formation)
schools.focus: Cosmogony based on the 32 Paths of Wisdom: 10 Sefirot (primordial numbers/dimensions) and 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

schools.name: Classical Theosophic Kabbalah (The Zohar)
schools.dates: Appeared c. 1280–1290 CE in Castile (attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; redacted by Moses de Leon)
schools.focus: The Ten Sefirot (Keter, Chokhmah, Binah, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod, Yesod, Malkhut/Shekhinah) manifesting the concealed Infinite (Ein Sof); human mitzvot unify masculine and feminine divine aspects (Yichud Kudesha Berikh Hu u-Shekhintei).

schools.name: Lurianic Kabbalah (Isaac Luria, The Ari)
focus: Tzimtzum (divine self-contraction creating a cosmic void for creation)
Shevirat Ha-Kelim (Shattering of the Vessels under intense primordial light)
Nitzotzot (holy divine sparks trapped within material reality and Klipot / shells of evil)
Tikkun Olam (cosmic restoration accomplished through prayer, halakhic observance, and mystical intention / Kavanah)

schools.name: Hasidism (Chasidut)
teachings: Panentheistic immanence of God in all things ('No place is void of Him')
Avodah be-Gashmiyyut (serving God through physical acts and mundane activities)
Joy (Simcha), ecstatic prayer (Devekut), and rejection of ascetic melancholy
The Tzaddik / Rebbe as spiritual intercessor and channel of divine blessing
Major branches: Chabad-Lubavitch, Satmar, Breslov, Ger, Belz, Vizhnitz

normative_boundary_clarification: Normative traditional Judaism holds that Kabbalah and Hasidism are esoteric interpretations subordinate to the binding legal obligations of Halakha; mystical speculation never suspends or abrogates dietary laws, Shabbat, or interpersonal commandments.
